note.text: A central bank has system-wide monetary responsibilities, distinct from an ordinary commercial bank’s customer business. It can conduct monetary policy, issue currency under its framework and support settlement arrangements. Central-bank reserves used between banks differ from customer deposit balances. Policy influences monetary and credit conditions rather than producing goods directly. Government taxation and expenditure are fiscal decisions, not the same activity as monetary policy. Institutional mandates vary, so a general comparison must be checked against the central bank actually being studied.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to distinguish monetary-policy and currency functions from commercial banking and fiscal decisions. Builds on: money, bank settlement and credit constraints. Leads to: a guided case study of BEAC and public finance.

sections.heading: Follow the local case
sections.text: Cameroon shares BEAC with other CEMAC states. Its stated missions include monetary policy, banknote and coin issue, foreign-exchange reserves and payment-system functioning. A commercial bank’s decision to credit a customer loan is different from BEAC issuing currency. Neither a policy announcement nor an accounting entry supplies every physical resource the economy needs.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Identify the institution and instrument before describing the effect. Separate cash issue, commercial-bank deposits and central-bank settlement balances. Distinguish government spending/tax decisions from monetary operations, and qualify any claim about policy outcomes.

pick.q: What can a policy announcement alone establish?

An announcement is not physical production.
Effects can differ by circumstance.
pick.y: Keep policy and measured outcome distinct.
